newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds barely changed after UK and U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds barely changed after UK and U.S. data.

text.p: Irish government bonds were barely changed in thin late trade on Wednesday after the release of key economic data in the UK and in the U.S. failed to ignite international markets, dealers said.
In the UK, January retail sales figures rose 0.6 percent to give a year-on-year figure of 4.6 percent, against a forecasted gain of 0.3 and 3.9 percent respectively.
The U.S. Labor Department reported the Consumer Price Index (CPI) rose 0.1 percent compared to a 0.3-percent jump in December. Economists had expected an overall CPI rise of 0.3 percent.

"It has been reasonably quiet. There were two key sets of data out. The UK data proved stronger than expected while the U.S. data was weak so they balanced each other out. We are trading very close to yesterday's closing levels," Riada's Padhraic Garvey said.

"There may be a case for saying that the short-end of the market has been over-bought. The short-end would be very vulnerable if sterling were to collapse or fall. But sterling is up today and that is supportive," he added.

By 1600 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 was down three pence from Tuesday's close at 103.12 to yield 5.71 percent while the key benchmark eight percent bond due 2006 was up five pence at 111.35 to yield 6.36 percent.
Dealers said Irish bonds were trading at 142 basis points over German bunds in the five year area and 92 basis points over Germany in the 10-year area.
The market was already looking towards next week and the release of CPI data and the Central Bank statement in Ireland as well as the Humphrey Hawkins testimony in the U.S.
